title: Router Loop
statement: A network packet follows a forwarding table: each of 10,000,000 routers names one next router, or "deliver". An embedded tester with almost no memory must decide whether a packet from router 0 gets stuck in a loop.

approaches.name: Floyd's cycle detection: one pointer moves one hop, the other two
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Detects the loop with two pointers and no memory of visited routers.

approaches.name: Follow the packet and store every router visited in a set
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but 10,000,000 stored routers do not fit the tester's memory.

approaches.name: Follow up to n hops; if not delivered, call it a loop
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Also correct with exactly n hops, but it always walks the full n hops even when the loop is tiny.

approaches.name: Change each visited table entry to a marker value
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Destroys the forwarding table, which the network still needs.

title: Middle of a Streamed Playlist
statement: A music app receives a playlist as a singly linked list of unknown length (up to 5,000,000 songs) and wants to start playback at the middle song, using constant extra memory.

approaches.name: Walk two pointers at one and two steps; when the fast one ends, the slow one is in the middle
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: One pass and no extra memory.

approaches.name: Count the songs, then walk half way
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct; it reads the list twice.

approaches.name: Copy the songs into an array and index the middle
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but stores up to 5,000,000 references.

approaches.name: Start at song 2,500,000
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: The actual length is unknown, so this is usually not the middle.

title: Duplicate Badge Number
statement: A read-only log holds 1,000,001 badge numbers, each between 1 and 1,000,000, so at least one number repeats; exactly one value repeats. The log cannot be changed and only a few variables of extra memory are allowed.
constraints: n + 1 values in 1..n; read-only; O(1) memory

approaches.name: Treat each value as a pointer to an index and run Floyd's cycle detection; the cycle's start is the duplicate
approaches.label: best
approaches.why: Two values point to the same index, which creates a cycle whose entrance is the repeated value.

approaches.name: Add each number to a hash set until one is already there
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Correct, but uses up to a million entries of memory.

approaches.name: Sort a copy and look for neighbours that are equal
approaches.label: valid
approaches.why: Needs a copy because the log is read-only.

approaches.name: Subtract 1 + 2 + … + n from the total
approaches.label: unsuitable
approaches.why: Only works if the duplicate appears exactly twice and every other number appears once, which the log does not promise.
